newsitem.title: USA: HBO leads list of Emmy nominations with 90.
newsitem.headline: HBO leads list of Emmy nominations with 90.

text.p: Cable television's Home Box Office channel stole the spotlight on Thursday as it grabbed 90 Emmy nominations, marking the first time a cable station received more nods than a major network.
Time-Warner's HBO, which received 16 nominations for "The Larry Sanders Show" and 12 for its civil rights miniseries "Miss Evers' Boys", edged out top rated network NBC.

But NBC, owned by General Electric was close with 89 nominations, including 22 for its top-rated hospital drama "ER", which led the nominations list for the third year in a row. CBS, which is owned by Westinghouse came in third place with 60 nominations, followed by Disney's ABC with 44 and Fox NCP.AX) with 19.
HBO's strong showing comes as network television ratings are declining in favour of a vast array of cable channels offering more innovative programming.

The Emmys, television's highest honours, are widely regarded as a measure of quality rather than popularity. Although HBO reaches a comparatively small number of U.S. households -- about 23 million -- it has consistently shined at the Emmys.

In 1993, HBO walked away with more awards than any network even though CBS received nearly twice as many nominations. Other HBO nominees this year were comedian Tracey Ullman's variety show, "Tracey Takes On", with eight; the miniseries "Gotti", with seven; and the made-for-TV movie "In The Gloaming", directed by paralysed actor Christopher Reeve, received five nominations.

Ellen DeGeneres, whose ABC comedy series "Ellen" made television history earlier this year when her character announced she was homosexual, was nominated for best actress for a comedy series -- one of five bids for that show.

But Richard Frank, president of the Academy of Television Arts & Sciences, said he saw that as a tribute to DeGeneres' talent rather than the groundbreaking episode. "Ellen is going to be a star for a long time. The entire gay issue is just another issue. She's an unbelievable talent," he said.

"Ellen", however, was not nominated for best comedy series. As it has for the past several years, NBC again dominated that category, receiving nominations for "Frasier", "Mad About You", "Seinfeld" and "3rd Rock From The Sun". The other best comedy series nomination went to HBO's "Larry Sanders Show".

Another NBC hit show, "Friends", did not receive a nomination, although it was erroneously named when a list of the main contenders was announced on national television. Frank said afterwards he had used last year's list of nominees during rehearsals, and then forgot to take "Friends" off the updated list.
"As soon as it ended, I knew I had made a mistake," he said.

This year's list of nominees also included several of Hollywood's major actors who have seldom appeared on television. Glenn Close was nominated for her work in "In The Gloaming" and Meryl Streep received a nod for her role in the ABC miniseries "First Do No Harm".
Actors Beau Bridges, Robert Duvall, Laurence Fishburne and Sidney Poitier were also nominated for their starring roles in various cable television miniseries and specials.
The shows nominated for best drama series were hospital dramas "Chicago Hope", and "ER", police dramas "Law & Order" and "NYPD Blue", and science fiction drama "The X-Files".

It was a case of rounding up the usual suspects in the category of best actor in a drama series. Those nominees were David Duchovny for "The X-Files", Anthony Edwards for "ER", Dennis Franz and Jimmy Smits for "NYPD Blue" and Sam Waterston for "Law & Order". But George Clooney, the other main male star of "ER", was not nominated this year.

Actresses nominated for their work in a drama series were Gillian Anderson for "The X-Files", Christine Lahti for "Chicago Hope", Julianna Margulies and Sherry Stringfield, for "ER", and Roma Downey for "Touched by an Angel." Stringfield left "ER" in midseason, saying she found the demands of a television series overwhelming.

Michael J. Fox was nominated for best actor in a comedy series for his work in "Spin City", along with Kelsey Grammer for "Frasier", John Lithgow for "3rd Rock from the Sun", Paul Reiser for "Mad About You", and Garry Shandling for "The Larry Sanders Show.

Besides DeGeneres, nominations for best actress in a comedy series went to Fran Drescher for "The Nanny", Helen Hunt for "Mad About You", Patricia Richardson for "Home Improvement" and Cybill Shepherd for "Cybill".
The 49th Annual Primetime Emmy Awards ceremony will take place on Sept. 14.
